name: MINDS
description: An open library of executable thinking systems. Source of truth for the MINDS registry. Edit this file, then run: python3 minds/_build/build.py

statuses.available: Research completed, sourced, operationalized, and reviewed. SKILL.md and SOURCES.md are published. Each SOURCES.md states how its principles were verified.
statuses.researching: Sources and framework currently being assembled. No executable skill yet.
statuses.planned: Included in the registry but not yet executable. No skill or sources published.

strategic-advantage.label: Strategic advantage
strategic-advantage.question: Where is advantage located, and can we act only where we hold it?

intelligence-and-deception.label: Intelligence and deception
intelligence-and-deception.question: What does each side know, and what does each side believe?

friction-and-uncertainty.label: Friction and uncertainty
friction-and-uncertainty.question: What will degrade between the plan and its execution?

center-of-gravity.label: Center of gravity
center-of-gravity.question: What source of strength, if lost, collapses the whole?

concentration-and-speed.label: Concentration and speed
concentration-and-speed.question: Can we mass decisive resources at the decisive point before others respond?

tempo-and-adaptation.label: Tempo and adaptation
tempo-and-adaptation.question: Who is observing, orienting, deciding, and acting faster?

power-and-legitimacy.label: Power and legitimacy
power-and-legitimacy.question: How is power actually gained, held, and lost here?

command-and-morale.label: Command and morale
command-and-morale.question: What sustains commitment and cohesion under pressure?

competitive-structure.label: Competitive structure
competitive-structure.question: What forces determine profitability in this arena?

positioning-and-tradeoffs.label: Positioning and trade-offs
positioning-and-tradeoffs.question: What are we choosing not to do?

monopoly-and-differentiation.label: Monopoly and differentiation
monopoly-and-differentiation.question: Are we escaping competition or trapped inside it?

disruption.label: Disruption
disruption.question: What changes when the basis of competition changes?

jobs-to-be-done.label: Jobs to be done
jobs-to-be-done.question: What progress is the customer actually trying to make?

strategic-inflection.label: Strategic inflection
strategic-inflection.question: Are the fundamentals of the business changing?

intrinsic-value.label: Intrinsic value
intrinsic-value.question: What is this worth, based on the cash it will produce?

margin-of-safety.label: Margin of safety
margin-of-safety.question: How wrong can we be and still be fine?

durable-advantage.label: Durable advantage
durable-advantage.question: What protects these economics from competition over time?

capital-allocation.label: Capital allocation
capital-allocation.question: Where does the next dollar earn the most, including returning it?

incentives.label: Incentives
incentives.question: What behavior do the incentives actually reward?

inversion.label: Inversion
inversion.question: What would guarantee failure, and how do we avoid it?

multidisciplinary-models.label: Multidisciplinary models
multidisciplinary-models.question: Which models from other disciplines explain what is happening?

customer-obsession.label: Customer obsession
customer-obsession.question: What does the customer need that no one is yet providing?

long-term-orientation.label: Long-term orientation
long-term-orientation.question: What looks different on a ten-year horizon?

decision-reversibility.label: Decision reversibility
decision-reversibility.question: Is this decision a one-way door or a two-way door?

business-definition.label: Business definition
business-definition.question: What is our business, who is the customer, and what does the customer value?

management-effectiveness.label: Management effectiveness
management-effectiveness.question: Are we doing the right things, not only doing things right?

managerial-leverage.label: Managerial leverage
managerial-leverage.question: Which activities produce the most output per unit of management attention?

organization-design.label: Organization design
organization-design.question: How should authority, coordination, and control be structured?

scale-and-cost.label: Scale and cost
scale-and-cost.question: Who has the lowest cost at scale, and why?

integration-and-consolidation.label: Integration and consolidation
integration-and-consolidation.question: Which parts of the value chain should be owned or combined?

scale-economies-shared.label: Scale economies shared
scale-economies-shared.question: Are scale savings returned to customers so the advantage compounds?

destination-analysis.label: Destination analysis
destination-analysis.question: Where will this be in ten or twenty years, and does today's behavior lead there?

cognitive-bias.label: Cognitive bias
cognitive-bias.question: Which systematic errors could distort this judgment?

base-rates.label: Base rates
base-rates.question: What usually happens in cases like this?

framing-effects.label: Framing effects
framing-effects.question: Would the choice change if the same facts were framed differently?

noise.label: Noise
noise.question: How much would this judgment vary between equally qualified judges?

bounded-rationality.label: Bounded rationality
bounded-rationality.question: What can the decision-makers realistically know and process?

decision-quality.label: Decision quality
decision-quality.question: Is this a good decision regardless of how the outcome turns out?

probabilistic-thinking.label: Probabilistic thinking
probabilistic-thinking.question: What are the plausible outcomes, and how likely is each?

fragility-and-tail-risk.label: Fragility and tail risk
fragility-and-tail-risk.question: What rare event would cause disproportionate harm?

optionality.label: Optionality
optionality.question: Where is the downside capped and the upside open?

skin-in-the-game.label: Skin in the game
skin-in-the-game.question: Who bears the consequences of being wrong?

first-principles.label: First principles
first-principles.question: Do we actually understand what is happening?

falsification.label: Falsification
falsification.question: What evidence would prove us wrong?

systematic-observation.label: Systematic observation
systematic-observation.question: What does careful, unprejudiced observation actually show?

selection-and-adaptation.label: Selection and adaptation
selection-and-adaptation.question: What is the environment selecting for?

information-and-signal.label: Information and signal
information-and-signal.question: What is signal, what is noise, and where is information lost?

abstraction.label: Abstraction
abstraction.question: What is the simplest version of this problem that keeps its essence?

good-explanations.label: Good explanations
good-explanations.question: Which explanation is hardest to vary while still accounting for the facts?

error-correction.label: Error correction
error-correction.question: How quickly can we detect and correct our mistakes?

system-vs-individual.label: System vs. individual
system-vs-individual.question: Is the person failing, or is the system producing the failure?

variation.label: Variation
variation.question: Is this a signal of real change or ordinary variation?

feedback-loops.label: Feedback loops
feedback-loops.question: What system is producing this behavior?

leverage-points.label: Leverage points
leverage-points.question: Where would a small intervention change the system most?

persuasion.label: Persuasion
persuasion.question: What principles of influence are shaping these choices?

rivalry-and-scapegoating.label: Rivalry and scapegoating
rivalry-and-scapegoating.question: Is conflict being resolved by blaming a scapegoat rather than the cause?

tactical-empathy.label: Tactical empathy
tactical-empathy.question: What does the other side feel, fear, and need to hear?

interests-over-positions.label: Interests over positions
interests-over-positions.question: What interests sit underneath each side's stated position?

alternatives-to-agreement.label: Alternatives to agreement
alternatives-to-agreement.question: What happens to each side if there is no deal?

brand-and-research.label: Brand and research
brand-and-research.question: What does research say the customer wants, and what does the brand promise?

measurable-advertising.label: Measurable advertising
measurable-advertising.question: What would a small, measurable test tell us before we scale?

creative-distinctiveness.label: Creative distinctiveness
creative-distinctiveness.question: Will anyone notice, and will it be remembered?

rhetoric.label: Rhetoric
rhetoric.question: Do we have credibility, emotional truth, and logic working together?

dichotomy-of-control.label: Dichotomy of control
dichotomy-of-control.question: What here is within our control, and what is not?

perspective.label: Perspective
perspective.question: How does this look from a wider view and a longer time?

adversity-rehearsal.label: Adversity rehearsal
adversity-rehearsal.question: Have we imagined the bad outcome clearly enough to be ready for it?

socratic-questioning.label: Socratic questioning
socratic-questioning.question: What do we mean by the words we are using, and do we actually know?

practical-wisdom.label: Practical wisdom
practical-wisdom.question: What is the right action, in this situation, for these people?

wildcard.why: Rehearsing the adverse outcome in advance can change which option feels acceptable.
Rivals often want the same things because they watch each other, not because the market demands it.
Asks whether resources are concentrated at the decisive point or spread too thinly.
Forces the thesis to name the evidence that would disprove it.
Tests whether the strategy's key terms, such as winning, customer, and market, are actually defined.
Treats the market as an environment that is changing what it selects for.
Examines what each side knows and believes before anyone sits down.
Looks for where information is lost, delayed, or distorted as it moves through the system.
Checks whether blame is settling on a convenient scapegoat instead of the cause.
Separates risks that can be acted on from risks that can only be prepared for.
Restating the problem in its most abstract form can expose solutions the specific framing hides.
Asks whether incentive schemes are blaming individuals for outcomes the system produces.
Brings self-command and a longer view to the pressures of leading others.
Suggests testing demand in small, measurable increments before committing.
Patient observation that deliberately records the facts that do not fit.

minds.name: Sun Tzu
minds.core_question: Where is advantage located?
questions: Can we win without direct confrontation?
What do we know about ourselves and our opponent?
Which terrain favors us?
may_underweight: the text is aphoristic, so application requires interpretation
minds.provenance_note: Authorship and dating of The Art of War are debated; the text is traditionally attributed to Sun Tzu and was likely compiled over time.
research_seeds: The Art of War (Sunzi bingfa), multiple translations

minds.name: Carl von Clausewitz
minds.core_question: What will friction do to this plan?
questions: What is the political purpose the effort serves?
Where is the opponent's center of gravity?
What is unknowable at the moment of decision?
best_used_for: plans that must survive contact with reality
may_underweight: commercial dynamics without a clear opponent
minds.provenance_note: On War was unfinished at his death and published posthumously; interpretations vary widely.

minds.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
minds.core_question: Where is the decisive point, and can we get there first?
questions: Are our resources concentrated or dispersed?
What does speed make possible that size cannot?
What happens if the decisive blow fails?
minds.provenance_note: Collections of 'Napoleon's maxims' were compiled by others after his death and are of mixed reliability. Frameworks must be derived from correspondence and documented campaigns, and labeled DERIVED.
research_seeds: Correspondance de Napoléon Ier (published under Napoleon III)
David G. Chandler, The Campaigns of Napoleon (1966), secondary

minds.name: Julius Caesar
minds.core_question: How do speed and political legitimacy reinforce each other?
questions: Who needs to believe in this effort, and why would they?
Where can decisive speed change the situation?
How is this being narrated to those whose support matters?
minds.provenance_note: Caesar's Commentaries are his own accounts and were written partly to persuade Roman audiences; they are primary sources but not neutral.

minds.name: Alexander the Great
minds.core_question: Where does bold, concentrated action break the opponent's structure?
questions: What does the leader's own example signal?
Where is the opponent structurally weak?
What happens after the conquest?
minds.provenance_note: No writings by Alexander survive. Everything is known through later accounts, chiefly Arrian and Plutarch, written centuries afterward. Any framework will be DERIVED from reported decisions, never DOCUMENTED in his own words.
research_seeds: Arrian, Anabasis of Alexander, secondary (2nd century CE)

minds.name: Niccolò Machiavelli
minds.core_question: How will people actually behave, not how should they?
questions: Who gains and who loses power from this?
What does fortune control, and what does preparation control?
Is this position held through fear, loyalty, or institutions?

minds.name: John Boyd
minds.core_question: Who is adapting faster?
questions: How current is our orientation to reality?
Where is our decision cycle slow?
What would disorient the opponent?
may_underweight: situations where speed is not the constraint
minds.provenance_note: Boyd published little in conventional form; his ideas are recorded mainly in briefing slides.
research_seeds: Frans Osinga, Science, Strategy and War (2007), secondary

minds.name: Warren Buffett
minds.core_question: What is this worth, and how certain can we be?
questions: How predictable are the economics?
What could permanently impair value?
Is the advantage durable?
Is management allocating capital rationally?
may_underweight: technology change outside the circle of competence

minds.name: Charlie Munger
minds.core_question: What are we missing?
questions: What would guarantee failure here?
How do the incentives drive behavior?
Which models from other fields apply?
best_used_for: checking a thesis for blind spots
research_seeds: Poor Charlie's Almanack (ed. Peter D. Kaufman)

minds.name: Peter Thiel
minds.core_question: Are we escaping competition or trapped inside it?
questions: What important truth do few people agree with?
Can this become a monopoly in a small market first?
Is this a definite plan or an indefinite hope?
may_underweight: competitive markets where differentiation is not available
research_seeds: Zero to One (2014, with Blake Masters)

minds.name: Jeff Bezos
minds.core_question: Is this a one-way door or a two-way door?
questions: What does the customer want that will not change in ten years?
Are we optimizing for long-term cash flow or short-term appearance?
Should this decision be fast or slow?

minds.name: Andy Grove
minds.core_question: Are the fundamentals of the business changing?
questions: Is this signal or noise?
What would a new management team do?
Which managerial activities have the highest leverage?

minds.name: Clayton Christensen
minds.core_question: What changes when the basis of competition changes?
questions: Are we overserving our best customers?
Who is entering from below with a simpler, cheaper offer?
What job is the customer hiring this for?
may_underweight: cases that do not fit the disruption pattern
research_seeds: The Innovator's Solution (2003, with Michael Raynor)
Competing Against Luck (2016, with Taddy Hall, Karen Dillon, and David S. Duncan)

minds.name: Michael Porter
minds.core_question: What determines the structure of competition?
questions: Where is the profit pool, and who captures it?
What trade-offs make our position hard to copy?
Which activities fit together into a system?

minds.name: Peter Drucker
minds.core_question: What is our business, and what does the customer value?
questions: What should we stop doing?
What results are we accountable for?
Where are the opportunities for innovation?

minds.name: John D. Rockefeller
minds.core_question: Who will be the lowest-cost producer at scale?
questions: Where does cost discipline create advantage?
Which parts of the chain should be controlled?
What does consolidation make possible?
minds.provenance_note: Much of the record is secondary. Business tactics must be separated from later reputation and myth.
research_seeds: Random Reminiscences of Men and Events (1909)

minds.name: Alfred P. Sloan
minds.core_question: How do we decentralize operations while coordinating control?
questions: Which decisions belong at the center, and which in the divisions?
How is performance measured across units?
Does the product line cover the market deliberately?

minds.name: Nomad Investment Partnership (Nick Sleep & Qais Zakaria)
minds.core_question: Is the business growing its advantage by giving more back to customers?
questions: What would management do with windfall profits?
How much does the customer save compared with what shareholders earn?
What is this business's destination, and is it on the road there?
may_underweight: businesses whose proposition is not based on price
minds.provenance_note: The letters are co-authored by Nick Sleep and Qais Zakaria. Attribute ideas to the partnership's letters, not to one author.
research_seeds: Nomad Investment Partnership Letters to Partners, 2001–2014 (full collection)

minds.name: Daniel Kahneman
minds.core_question: Which biases could distort this judgment?
questions: What is the outside view?
Are we answering an easier question than the one asked?
How much would independent judges disagree?
research_seeds: Noise (2021, with Olivier Sibony and Cass R. Sunstein)
Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases (Science, 1974, with Amos Tversky)

minds.name: Amos Tversky
minds.core_question: How is the framing shaping the choice?
questions: Would the preference reverse under a different description?
Are losses being weighed more heavily than equal gains?
What heuristic is producing this estimate?
minds.provenance_note: Much of Tversky's work is co-authored with Daniel Kahneman. The skill must attribute joint work accurately.
research_seeds: The Framing of Decisions and the Psychology of Choice (Science, 1981, with Daniel Kahneman)

minds.name: Herbert Simon
minds.core_question: What can the decision-makers realistically know and process?
questions: Where is attention the scarce resource?
Is 'good enough' the right standard here?
How does the organization's structure shape its decisions?

minds.name: Annie Duke
minds.core_question: Is this a good decision regardless of how it turns out?
questions: How confident are we, in percentages?
Are we judging past decisions by their outcomes?
What would make us quit, decided in advance?
may_underweight: domains where probabilities cannot be estimated meaningfully

minds.name: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
minds.core_question: What happens in the tail?
questions: Is this fragile, robust, or antifragile?
Where is the downside capped and the upside open?
Who bears the cost of being wrong?

minds.name: Richard Feynman
minds.core_question: Do we actually understand what is happening?
questions: Could we explain this simply?
Are we fooling ourselves?
What does the data say, independent of what we want?
may_underweight: decisions that cannot wait for understanding
research_seeds: Appendix F to the Rogers Commission Report (1986)

minds.name: Charles Darwin
minds.core_question: What is the environment selecting for?
questions: Which variations survive, and why?
What changed in the environment?
Which facts do not fit our theory?
minds.provenance_note: Applying evolutionary ideas to business is an analogy. The skill must mark all such transfers as OPERATIONALIZED, not as Darwin's claims.

minds.name: Francis Bacon
minds.core_question: Which errors of mind are shaping what we see?
questions: What would careful, organized observation show?
Are we generalizing too quickly?
Which inherited assumptions are we treating as facts?
may_underweight: the role of theory in guiding observation

minds.name: Karl Popper
minds.core_question: What evidence would prove us wrong?
questions: Is this claim falsifiable?
Have we tried to refute it, or only to confirm it?
What bold conjecture would explain more?
may_underweight: decisions that require action before tests are possible
research_seeds: The Logic of Scientific Discovery (1934; English 1959)

minds.name: Claude Shannon
minds.core_question: What is signal, and what is noise?
questions: What is the simplest abstract form of this problem?
Where is information being lost?
What is the capacity of this channel?
minds.provenance_note: Shannon's information theory deliberately excludes meaning. Applying it to organizations is an analogy and must be labeled OPERATIONALIZED.
research_seeds: A Mathematical Theory of Communication (Bell System Technical Journal, 1948)

minds.name: David Deutsch
minds.core_question: What is the best explanation, and is it hard to vary?
questions: Would this explanation survive if its details were changed arbitrarily?
Is this problem treated as soluble, or as a fixed limit?
What mechanism lets us find and fix our errors?
best_used_for: strategies that rest on a theory of why
institutions that must correct their own mistakes
may_underweight: probabilistic and Bayesian framings, which this framework is skeptical of
minds.provenance_note: Deutsch builds explicitly on Karl Popper. The skill must distinguish Deutsch's own extensions from Popper's original ideas.

minds.name: W. Edwards Deming
minds.core_question: Is the person failing, or is the system producing the failure?
questions: Is this common-cause or special-cause variation?
What does the process reliably produce?
Are we blaming people for outcomes the system produces?

minds.name: Donella Meadows
minds.core_question: What system is producing this behavior?
questions: Which feedback loops dominate?
Where are the delays?
Where is the highest-leverage intervention?
research_seeds: Thinking in Systems (2008, ed. Diana Wright)
Leverage Points: Places to Intervene in a System (1999)

minds.name: Robert Cialdini
minds.core_question: What principles of influence are shaping these choices?
questions: What social proof are buyers seeing?
What commitments have already been made?
What happens in the moment before the message?
may_underweight: long-run trust effects of heavy-handed tactics

minds.name: René Girard
minds.core_question: Whose desire is being imitated?
questions: Are rivals converging because they watch each other?
Is conflict escalating through imitation?
Who is being made the scapegoat?
minds.provenance_note: Girard wrote about literature, religion, and anthropology. Applying mimetic theory to markets is an extension and must be labeled OPERATIONALIZED.
research_seeds: Things Hidden Since the Foundation of the World (1978)

minds.name: Chris Voss
minds.core_question: What does the other side need to hear to feel understood?
questions: What are they afraid of?
Which calibrated question would reveal more?
What is unsaid?
research_seeds: Never Split the Difference (2016, with Tahl Raz)

minds.name: Roger Fisher
minds.core_question: What interests sit underneath the positions?
questions: What is each side's best alternative to a negotiated agreement?
Which options create value for both sides?
What objective criteria could settle this?
minds.provenance_note: Getting to Yes is co-authored with William Ury (and Bruce Patton in later editions); attribute accordingly.
research_seeds: Getting to Yes (1981, with William Ury)

minds.name: David Ogilvy
minds.core_question: What does the customer need to know to choose us?
questions: What does research say about the buyer?
Is the promise specific and believable?
Is this building the brand over time?
may_underweight: channels his era did not have

minds.name: Claude Hopkins
minds.core_question: What does the test say?
questions: Can this be measured before it is scaled?
What is the cost per result?
What specific claim drives response?
may_underweight: brand effects that resist short-term measurement

minds.name: Bill Bernbach
minds.core_question: Will anyone notice, and will anyone remember?
questions: Is this honest and distinctive?
Does the idea respect the audience?
Does it look like everything else?
minds.provenance_note: Bernbach wrote little at length. Many quotations attributed to him are unverified, so sources must be checked with care.
research_seeds: Bob Levenson, Bill Bernbach's Book (1987), secondary

minds.name: Marcus Aurelius
minds.core_question: What does duty require here, seen from a wider view?
questions: What is within my power to do well?
How small is this, measured against the whole?
What is the obstacle teaching?
minds.provenance_note: Meditations was written as private notes, not for publication.

minds.name: Seneca
minds.core_question: Have we rehearsed the bad outcome?
questions: What would we do if the worst happened?
Are we spending time on what matters?
Is fear larger than the actual risk?
research_seeds: Letters to Lucilius (Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium)

minds.name: Epictetus
minds.core_question: What is within our control, and what is not?
questions: Are we distressed by events or by our judgments about them?
Where should effort go?
What are we treating as ours that is not?
minds.provenance_note: Epictetus wrote nothing himself. His teachings were recorded by his student Arrian.

minds.name: Socrates
minds.core_question: Do we actually know what we think we know?
questions: What do we mean by this term?
What follows if this is true?
Where does our reasoning contradict itself?
minds.provenance_note: Socrates wrote nothing. He is known through Plato, Xenophon, and Aristophanes, and separating Socrates from Plato is a long-standing scholarly problem.

minds.name: Aristotle
minds.core_question: What is the right action, for these people, in this situation?
questions: What is the end this serves?
Where is the mean between excess and deficiency?
Are credibility, emotion, and argument aligned?
minds.provenance_note: The surviving works are largely lecture notes, compiled and edited after his death.
